issues.failure_explanation: For the linear SDE dU=(FU+b)dt+L dW with F=-(\gamma/\kappa)(I-(\beta/\kappa)P_t C^{-1}), the covariance obeys \dot\Sigma=F\Sigma+\Sigma F^T+LL^T. The proof writes the second term as \Sigma_t F (i.e. \Sigma_t P_t C^{-1}) instead of \Sigma_t F^T = \Sigma_t C^{-1} P_t. Since P_t and C_{*,t}^{-1} are symmetric but need not commute (e.g. for a constant K not commuting with \Sigma, \Sigma_t), the stated right-hand side of the ODE is not even symmetric, so the lemma's covariance ODE is false in the generality claimed (it is only correct when P_t and C_{*,t} commute).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \Sigma_t P_t C_{*,t}^{-1} by \Sigma_t C_{*,t}^{-1} P_t in eq:lmm:lcbs:gauss:moments:evol-C and in the preceding proof line (transpose of the drift matrix).
issues.overall_effect: The covariance ODE as stated is incorrect for preconditioners that do not commute with \Sigma and \Sigma_t, including the listed constant-K case. The later uses (Corollary cor:lcbs:gauss:gamma with \Sigma_t=\Sigma and commuting preconditioners; Lemma lmm:compare:cbs:equiv where P_tC^{-1} is a scalar multiple of I) fall in the commuting regime and remain valid.
issues.title: Covariance ODE in Lemma on Gaussian moments has wrong (non-transposed) second term for non-commuting preconditioners
issues.why_classification: A local, forced correction (transposing one factor) restores the lemma in full generality; all downstream results use the commuting case and are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \dot U_t = -\frac\gamma\kappa\Bigl(U_t - \mu_{\beta,\kappa\mathbf C_{U,t}/\beta}(\rho_t; U_t)\Bigr) + \nabla_u \cdot \mathbf C_{U,t} + \sqrt{2\mathbf C_{U,t}}\,\dot W_t.

issues.failure_explanation: The localized CBS dynamics depend on the free parameter \gamma, and the moment ODEs (eq:lmm:lcbs:gauss:moments) scale with \gamma. The lemma's parameter list fixes \alpha,\kappa,\beta,\lambda but not \gamma, yet the proof silently uses \gamma=2\alpha'/(\alpha'+1) (the value from eq:cor:lcbs:gauss:gamma:gamma-Cw for these parameters). For any other \gamma the drift coefficient \gamma/\kappa changes and the claimed identities m_t=m'_{ct}, \Sigma_t=\Sigma'_{ct} fail, so the statement as written is false without this extra hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add \gamma = 2\alpha'/(\alpha'+1) (equivalently, the value given by eq:cor:lcbs:gauss:gamma:gamma-Cw) to the parameter list eq:lmm:compare:cbs:equiv:params.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lmm:compare:cbs:equiv is unsupported as stated; it holds only under the unstated choice \gamma=2\alpha'/(\alpha'+1).
issues.title: Equivalence lemma with CBS omits the required value of γ from its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The omitted hypothesis is exactly what the proof uses and is already derivable from the corollary; adding it preserves the result entirely.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a weighted covariance $\mathbf C_{U,t} = \mathcal C_{\alpha, \lambda \mathcal C(\rho_t)}(\rho_t; U_t)$ with scalars $\alpha\ge0$ and $\lambda > 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is asserted for all \alpha'>0 and \alpha>0, but \lambda=\alpha'/(\alpha-\alpha') is undefined when \alpha=\alpha' and negative when \alpha<\alpha', whereas the weighted covariance preconditioner is defined only for \lambda>0 (for \lambda<0 the localization weight \exp(+|v-u|^2/(2|\lambda|)) is unbounded and the preconditioner is not a well-defined object for general laws). The stated quantifier over \alpha therefore includes parameter choices for which the localized CBS dynamics in the lemma are not defined by the paper's own definitions.

failure_location.quote: For any choice of the CBS parameter\footnote{We write $\alpha'$ for the CBS parameter to distinguish it from the $\alpha$ parameter of localized CBS.} $\alpha' > 0$ and with localized CBS parameters

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the hypothesis to \alpha>\alpha' (optionally noting \alpha=\alpha' corresponds to \lambda=\infty, i.e. the \mathcal C_\alpha preconditioner).
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's scope is overstated; it is meaningful only for \alpha>\alpha' (with \alpha=\alpha' recoverable as the \lambda=\infty limit).
issues.title: Equivalence lemma allows α ≤ α′, making λ undefined or negative contrary to the preconditioner's definition
issues.why_classification: A one-line restriction of the parameter range fixes the statement; the substantive equivalence with CBS for the admissible regime is unaffected.
